title: Constrained-output safety probes and graceful-fallback playbook for streaming + tool calls
creator: Leah Chen
description:
Goal: Build a focused test harness and playbook that validates JSON-mode enforcement across streaming outputs and interleaved tool/function calls, exercises constrained-decoding failure modes, and verifies schema-adherence and migration behaviors under realistic production stressors.

Background: We’ve had intermittent customer reports where structured-output consumers receive partial JSON blobs (streamed truncation), interleaved toolcall metadata, or slightly-migrated schema versions that break downstream parsers. This ticket centralizes acceptance criteria and a reproducible harness for: streaming partial-emits, tool-call interleaving, backpressure-induced truncation, and schema version compatibility.

Proposed scope (deliverables):
- A test harness that can replay traffic scenarios with: streaming responses, scheduled tool/function calls (tool-call metadata interleaved into stream), and simulated network backpressure. The harness should produce deterministic seeds for fuzzing.
- A set of canonical prompt fixtures (golden prompts) covering: optional-field migrations, array-to-object transitions, enum expansion, and nullable-to-non-nullable flips. Each fixture includes the expected canonical JSON path assertions.
- Constrained-decoding failure simulation: deterministic injection of token-level noise to exercise decoder backoff and the fallback decoder path.
- Graceful-repair scenarios: automated repair attempts (skeleton-fill, trailing-brace append, partial-emit re-request) and a policy matrix that determines when to auto-repair vs. surface an error.
- Observability and telemetry: Add assertions for emitted metrics (schema_violation_count, stream_reconstruction_attempts, toolcall_interleave_rate, constrained_decoder_backoffs) and link to a dashboard for nightly regression detection.
- Runbook and API contract tests: a short playbook for SRE/Support to triage a customer-facing schema break, and a CI job that runs the harness on every runtime and console release.

Non-goals: implementing parser-level changes in all SDKs (we will add test vectors and an SDK checklist but separate tickets will track SDK updates).

Acceptance criteria (high-level):
1) Harness can reproduce 8 predefined scenarios deterministically: three streaming truncation variants, two interleaved tool-call variants, two schema-migration variants, one constrained-decoder noise stress.
2) For each scenario, the harness emits a pass/fail and a standardized artifact bundle (raw stream capture, reassembly log, repair attempt log, assertion results) and uploads to CI artifacts.
3) CI job executes harness nightly and on PRs touching decoder/canonicalizer/runtime changes; failing scenarios open an automated Linear ticket with attached artifacts.
4) Dashboard shows per-build regression markers for the four metrics defined in scope.

Notes on design decisions:
- Use seeded pseudo-random token perturbations (not true randomness) to ensure reproducible constrained-decoding failures.
- Prefer lightweight repair heuristics (append missing bracket, attempt minimal trailing-field fill) as a first-line auto-repair; any repair that mutates semantics must be opt-in per-route.
- Tool-calls are modeled as tagged events inserted into the byte-stream (metadata format: TOOLCALL::{"name":"...","id":"...","payload":"..."}); the reassembly layer must strip or surface these events according to contract.

Attached artifacts and links:
- Design spec (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/Structured+Output+Safety+Playbook
- Prototype harness repo (internal GH): https://github.com/redwood-inference/so-harness/pull/67
- Golden prompt set (GCS): gs://redwood-testdata/structured-output/golden-prompts/2025-02-12.tar.gz
- Dashboard (Kibana): https://kibana.redwood.local/d/harness/structured-output-regressions

Operational impact: Adds one nightly CI job and an optional presubmit check for changes touching constrained-decoder and stream-reassembly. Estimated infra cost: small (additional build minutes + storage for artifacts).
acceptance_criteria: Harness reproduces 8 predefined deterministic scenarios and uploads artifact bundles for each
CI job runs harness nightly and on relevant PRs; failures create automated tickets
Dashboard reports schema_violation_count, stream_reconstruction_attempts, toolcall_interleave_rate, constrained_decoder_backoffs
Runbook documented and linked; SRE able to triage a failing scenario in <30 minutes
